nodes.name: NF pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Before usage, the NF was immersed in 3 M HCl for 5 min to improve its hydrophilicity and then rinsed with DI water several times.
nodes.source_text: Before usage, the NF was immersed in 3 M HCl for 5 min to improve its hydrophilicity and then rinsed with DI water several times.

nodes.name: NiFe LDH spontaneous growth
nodes.procedure: Following this pretreatment, pieces of NF (1.5 × 3 cm²) were immersed in 10 mL solution of 0.15 M Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O and 0.15 M FeSO₄·7H₂O at room temperature for different amounts of time (from 1 to 5 h). Finally, the NF pieces were removed and placed on filter paper to dry at room temperature. The resulting electrodes are denoted as NF/NiFe LDH.

nodes.name: CoFe LDH spontaneous growth
nodes.procedure: The growth of CoFe LDH and FeOOH on the surface of NF generally follows the same procedure as that for NF/NiFe LDH. Solutions of 0.15 M Co(NO3)2·6H2O + 0.15 M FeSO4·7H2O were employed as the reaction solutions for CoFe LDH. The reaction time for both CoFe LDH and FeOOH was set at 2 h.

nodes.description: OER performance comparison in 1 M KOH (includes NF, NF/IrO2 benchmarks)
nodes.source_text: NF/NiFe LDH requires only a very low overpotential of 202 mV to reach a current density of 10 mA/cm2, while overpotentials of 304 mV and 331 mV are required for NF/IrO2 and nickel foam... To achieve higher current densities of 100, 200, and 500 mA/cm2, the needed overpotentials are 237, 251, and 274 mV... NF/NiFe LDH exhibits the lowest Tafel slope of 32.8 mV/dec... NF/NiFe LDH shows the lowest charge transfer resistance (Rct) of about 0.564 Ω

nodes.evidence_snippet: After the NF was immersed in the solution of 0.15 M Fe2+ and 0.15 M Ni2+ for 2 h, a thin layer of nanosheets was uniformly grown on its surface, as shown in Fig. 1c and d.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM verifies the typical nanosheet structure of NiFe LDH; HRTEM shows lattice fringes with interplanar distance of 0.25 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1e and f, the typical nanosheet structure of NiFe LDH was verified at different magnifications. The high-resolution TEM image displayed in Fig. 1h shows the lattice fringes of the NiFe LDH planes with an interplanar distances of 0.25 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows well-resolved diffraction rings corresponding to the (012), (015) and (113) planes of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selective area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern displayed in Fig. 1g shows well-resolved diffraction rings corresponding to the (012), (015) and (113) planes of NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping proves uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O; map sum spectrum shows Ni/Fe ratio of about 5/3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To determine the elemental distribution in these samples, energy-dispersive X-ray microscopy (EDX) elemental mapping was conducted... The EDX elemental mapping images clearly prove the uniform distribution of elemental Ni, Fe, and O. Moreover, the map sum spectrum of EDX mapping displayed in Fig S5 shows that the Ni/Fe ratio of our sample is about 5/3.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 855.8 eV and 873.6 eV indicating Ni2+; Fe 2p peaks at 713.1 eV and 725.5 eV indicating Fe3+; O 1s peaks at 531.0 eV (M-O) and 532.7 eV (M-OH).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 2a, the peaks at 855.8 and 873.6 eV correspond to the Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 orbits, respectively... indicating the Ni2+ oxidation state. The Fe 2p spectrum (Fig. 2b) shows two dominant peaks at 713.1 eV (Fe 2p3/2) and 725.5 eV (Fe 2p1/2)... which are the typical characteristics of the Fe3+ oxidation state. The O 1s spectrum in Fig. 2c displays metal-O (M-O) and metal-OH (M-OH) peaks located at 531.0 and 532.7 eV, respectively.
